---
title: "Sample RMS energy onto a TR grid"
subtitle: "Extract `audio.rms`, then resample it to a 2 s scan grid whose first volume is 0.67 s before the soundtrack starts."
sidebar: cookbook
---

## Use when

You have a soundtrack and want one RMS energy value per fMRI volume. The scan
starts first; the audio begins a fraction of a second later. This page uses
TR = 2 s and a stimulus onset of 0.67 s on the scan clock.

`extract_features()` keeps RMS on its native hop grid. Sampling onto TRs is a
second, explicit step: `build_experiment_grid()` plus
`query_feature_window_tr()`.

The executed cells below use a short synthetic WAV so the docs site can render
without a large local recording. The same calls apply to a file such as
`data/stimuli/DownTheRabbitHoleFinal_mono_exp120_NR16_pad.wav`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update(
    {
        "figure.facecolor": "#111827",
        "axes.facecolor": "#111827",
        "axes.edgecolor": "#9ca3af",
        "axes.labelcolor": "#e5e7eb",
        "axes.titlecolor": "#f9fafb",
        "xtick.color": "#d1d5db",
        "ytick.color": "#d1d5db",
        "grid.color": "#374151",
        "text.color": "#f9fafb",
        "legend.facecolor": "#111827",
        "legend.edgecolor": "#4b5563",
    }
)
```

```{python}
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from natural_features import build_experiment_grid, extract_features, query_feature_window_tr

tr_s = 2.0
stim_onset_s = 0.67
sr_hz = 8000
duration_s = 16.0

t = np.arange(int(duration_s * sr_hz), dtype=np.float32) / sr_hz
envelope = np.full(t.shape, 0.03, dtype=np.float32)
envelope[(t >= 4.0) & (t < 10.0)] = 0.35
samples = envelope * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * 220.0 * t)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    wav_path = Path(tmp) / "soundtrack.wav"
    pcm = np.asarray(np.clip(samples, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0, dtype="<i2")
    with wave.open(str(wav_path), "wb") as wav:
        wav.setnchannels(1)
        wav.setsampwidth(2)
        wav.setframerate(sr_hz)
        wav.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())

    result = extract_features(wav_path, features=["audio.rms"])

rms = result.features["audio.rms"]
n_trs = int(np.ceil((stim_onset_s + duration_s) / tr_s))
grid = build_experiment_grid(
    tr_s=tr_s,
    n_trs_by_run=[n_trs],
    run_starts_s=[0.0],
    feature_t0_s=stim_onset_s,
)
sampled = query_feature_window_tr(
    rms,
    grid,
    run_index=1,
    t_start_s=0.0,
    t_end_s=n_trs * tr_s,
    relative_to_run=True,
    method="mean",
    output_time="run_relative",
)
```

## What the two grids are

`feature_t0_s=0.67` means audio t = 0 is scan t = 0.67 s. The first TR is still
at scan t = 0. On the audio clock that sample sits at −0.67 s, so the first
volume averages whatever RMS rows fall in that TR window, including the start
of the soundtrack.

```{python}
{
    "native_hop_s": rms.timebase.hop_s,
    "native_rows": int(rms.values.shape[0]),
    "native_first_times_s": rms.times_s[:3].tolist(),
    "n_trs": n_trs,
    "tr_times_s": sampled.times_s.tolist(),
    "audio_time_of_first_tr_s": float(sampled.times_s[0] - stim_onset_s),
    "tr_rms": sampled.values[:, 0].tolist(),
}
```

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 3.2))
ax.plot(rms.times_s + stim_onset_s, rms.values[:, 0], color="#93c5fd", lw=1.0, label="native RMS (scan clock)")
ax.plot(sampled.times_s, sampled.values[:, 0], color="#fbbf24", marker="o", lw=1.6, label="TR-sampled RMS")
ax.axvline(stim_onset_s, color="#f9a8d4", ls="--", lw=1.0, label="audio t=0")
ax.set_xlabel("scan time (s)")
ax.set_ylabel("RMS")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.35)
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig
```

The yellow points are one mean RMS value per 2 s TR. The loud block occupies
audio 4–10 s, which is scan 4.67–10.67 s, so the points at 6 s, 8 s, and 10 s
are the high ones.

`method="mean"` averages native RMS rows whose times fall in `[t - TR/2, t + TR/2)`.
Pass `method="linear"` if you want interpolation onto the TR instants instead
of bin averaging.

## Point the same calls at a local soundtrack

The WAV is not in the repository. Copy it to `data/stimuli/` or pass its path:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from natural_features import build_experiment_grid, extract_features, query_feature_window_tr

wav_path = Path("data/stimuli/DownTheRabbitHoleFinal_mono_exp120_NR16_pad.wav")
tr_s = 2.0
stim_onset_s = 0.67

result = extract_features(wav_path, features=["audio.rms"])
rms = result.features["audio.rms"]
audio = result.inputs["audio"]
duration_s = audio.samples.shape[0] / audio.sr_hz
n_trs = int(np.ceil((stim_onset_s + duration_s) / tr_s))

grid = build_experiment_grid(
    tr_s=tr_s,
    n_trs_by_run=[n_trs],
    run_starts_s=[0.0],
    feature_t0_s=stim_onset_s,
)
sampled = query_feature_window_tr(
    rms,
    grid,
    run_index=1,
    t_start_s=0.0,
    t_end_s=n_trs * tr_s,
    relative_to_run=True,
    method="mean",
    output_time="run_relative",
)
```

A command-line wrapper lives at `examples/rms_energy_to_tr_grid.py`.

If the WAV is already padded so file t = 0 equals scan t = 0, set
`stim_onset_s` / `feature_t0_s` to `0.0`.

## When not to resample yet

If the next step is hemodynamic convolution, keep `rms` on its native hop and
hand it downstream as a `TemporalPayload`. TR sampling then happens after the
HRF, in the modeling library. This page is for the case where the TR-sampled
energy series is the object you want.
